title: Premium Accounting Manual: Premium Credits by Reason and Refunds on Premium Billing Accounts
content:
**Clause 1 — every credit has a reason and a product line.** A premium credit on a Premium Billing Accounts arrangement is booked for a definite reason and a definite product line.

| Credit reason | What it credits |
|---|---|
| Free-look refund | every premium paid for the cancelled plan |
| Termination (unearned months) | see the retired wording below |
| Prepay unearned | the remaining whole months of an annual prepay at the discounted monthly rate (the arrangement's prepay unearned basis) |
| Plan-change difference | see the retired wording below |
| Overpayment | payments beyond what was billed |
| APTC reconciliation | advance premium tax credit adjustments notified by the exchange |
| Retro termination | group terminations reported retroactively, within the retro limit (clause 2) |

> **Former wording — no longer in force in its general form:** "A termination credit credits premium billed for whole coverage months after the termination month (the termination credit basis), never a partial month."
> It continues for every termination credit other than two: the termination credit for a vision plan unit funded by an individual-market account whose subscriber enrollment ended by voluntary termination, and the termination credit for an orthodontic rider funded by the account that has ended. Each of those two is settled under its own Premium Billing Accounts credit rule. Every other termination credit is the premium billed for whole coverage months after the termination month, never a partial month.

> **Former wording — no longer in force in its general form:** "A plan-change difference credit credits the difference when a plan change lowers premium already billed."
> It continues for every plan-change difference credit other than the tier-difference credit for a dental plan unit whose coverage tier dropped because a dependent's dental enrollment ended for loss of eligibility, which is settled under its own Premium Billing Accounts credit rule. Every other plan-change difference credit is the difference when a plan change lowers premium already billed.

**Clause 2 — retroactive group terminations.** A group may report a member's termination retroactively, but a retro termination credit may be given only for coverage months that begin within the retro termination limit before the date the group reported the termination; earlier months stay billed. The retro limit is the arrangement's retro termination limit in calendar days, counted back from the date the termination is reported, and a month whose first day falls on or after the resulting date can be credited. The coverage months examined are those recorded on the account's own ledger for the account being credited.

*Boundary case (hypothetical, 60-day limit).* A termination reported on 15 May: 60 calendar days back is 16 March. The months beginning 1 April and 1 May can be credited; the month beginning 1 March began before 16 March and stays billed. Had the termination been reported on 30 April, 60 days back would be 1 March, and the month beginning 1 March — its first day falling on that date — could be credited.

**Clause 3 — refunds.** A refund pays out a credit under the credit-balance rules and references the credit it pays. A refund is never issued for coverage months in which a claim was paid for the person under the credited plan, except for a free-look cancellation, which requires that no claim was paid at all.

superseded_clauses: termination_unearned credits premium billed for whole coverage months after the termination month (termination_credit_basis), never a partial month
plan_change_difference credits the difference when a plan change lowers premium already billed
